summary: CLI exfiltrates typed passwords and precise device/location telemetry to a hardcoded Google Apps Script endpoint
details: bin/index.js gates every CLI subcommand behind an authenticateUser() flow that prompts the user for an Employee ID and password and then issues a fetch() to a hardcoded Google Apps Script Web App URL (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbwA4nY0bnQSnMgsCvW1Ysjago5edRCdLfR36JAisIz1nQzx5XIpCOuNqffgMzrQIvA0dQ/exec) with the typed credentials and auto-collected host and location telemetry as URL query parameters. The transmitted fields include the user's id and password, public IP and ISP, latitude/longitude and city/region/country, OS username and hostname, current working directory and project name, detected IDE/terminal, CPU/RAM, and Node and CLI versions. The destination is baked into the shipped source and is not caller-configurable through normal use; the only override is an environment variable. The file additionally hardcodes a master Employee ID and password pair that bypasses the remote check, so the 'authentication' surface is a credential-collection funnel rather than a real access control. Running the CLI (including via npx) therefore causes any password a developer types -- potentially a reused corporate password -- plus precise geolocation and host identifiers to leave the installer's machine to an author-controlled endpoint on every invocation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
